newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan's Q4 earnings hurt by weak metal prices.
newsitem.headline: Alcan's Q4 earnings hurt by weak metal prices.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd., the world's second biggest aluminum producer, said on Thursday its fourth-quarter earnings rose from a year earlier but were hurt by weak metal prices.
Montreal-based Alcan reported a fourth-quarter profit of $72 million or $0.31 a share, compared with year-earlier net earnings of $46 million or $0.17 a share.
Alcan's 1995 fourth quarter was hurt by a strike at its Quebec operations, which cut earnings by about $70 million.
The company said that for the 1996 fourth quarter its average realized price on fabricated products was US$181 a metric ton lower than in the third quarter, due mainly to weaker metal prices.

Sales in the fourth quarter fell to $1.8 billion from $2.2 billion a year earlier, reflecting 1996 disposals of a number of Alcan's fabrication businesses in the United Kingdom, Australia and North America.
For the full year, Alcan earnings rose to $410 million or $1.74 a share from $263 million or $1.06 a share in 1995.
Sales declined for the year to $7.6 billion from $9.3 billion in 1995.
Alcan Chief Executive Jacques Bougie noted that 1996 results reflected a "difficult business environment."
"Slower economic growth and inventory reductions by customers kept primary metal prices under pressure through most of the year," Bougie said in a statement.
Alcan shares fell C$0.05 to C$49.30 on the Toronto Stock Exchange and were up 12.5 cents to $36.875 in afternoon trading on Thursday on the New York Stock Exchange.
